title: On-Prem Kubernetes Rolling Upgrade Playbook and Terraform Module Notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for performing rolling control-plane and node upgrades for on-prem Kubernetes clusters managed for Redwood Private deployments. It contains runbook steps, Terraform module notes, pre-check lists, validation commands, and rollback approaches for both bare-metal and vSphere flavors.

Scope and assumptions:
- Clusters are provisioned with our terraform modules (module versions noted below).
- kubeadm is the control-plane bootstrap mechanism; kubelet is system-managed.
- CRI: containerd (version pinned in module).
- CNI: Calico in most clusters; some legacy clusters use Flannel — note CNI differences in validation section.
- Etcd: stacked on control-plane nodes (default).
- Backup strategy: etcd snapshots to S3-compatible object store (minio) prior to major control-plane upgrades.

High-level upgrade plan (rolling):
1) Pre-upgrade checks (see checklist).
2) Snapshot etcd and verify snapshot restoration candidate.
3) Upgrade control-plane nodes one at a time (kubeadm upgrade apply on target version, drain worker workloads if control-plane workloads are present).
4) Validate cluster health (component status, API server latency, scheduler, controller-manager).
5) Upgrade kube-proxy and CNI if required.
6) Roll nodes through a cordon/drain -> kubelet package -> reboot (if needed) -> uncordon cycle in small batches.
7) Run post-upgrade validation suite (smoke tests + perf spot checks).

Pre-upgrade checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm maintenance window with customer + SRE on-call.
- [ ] Confirm backup of etcd: run etcdctl snapshot save and verify size/checksum.
- [ ] Ensure Terraform state is accessible and writable.
- [ ] Verify available capacity to drain nodes (pod disruption budgets, extra spare nodes).
- [ ] Verify current kubeadm version and target version compatibility (see version skew table below).
- [ ] Collect current metrics and traces baseline (latency, QPS, token consumption).
- [ ] Alerting: suppress noisy alerts for the window or set runbook annotations.

Terraform module notes (current WIP):
- module: private-k8s-cluster (v0.12.3-wip)
  - variables added in this branch: control_plane_upgrade_strategy = "kubeadm-rolling", spare_node_pool_size = 2
  - outputs: cluster_etcd_endpoint, bootstrap_token_secret, node_pool_ids
  - known issues: vsphere provisioning race when creating distributed switch portgroups; added depends_on workaround for now.
- module: vsphere-hosts (v0.6.1)
  - vsphere_vm_template_id is required when using snapshot-based OS images; workspace uses ubuntu-22.04-k8s-1.27 image currently.
  - We added a lifecycle ignore_changes for spec.mac_address to avoid re-provision churn on NICs.
- module: baremetal-provisioner (v0.3.0-beta)
  - uses iPXE + TFTP to provision. TODO: replace inline cloud-init with pre-seeded image to speed reprovision.

Terraform tips for upgrades:
- Keep terraform plan output saved as artifact (attach to ticket).
- Use -target hacks sparingly; prefer module version bump with safe drift reconciliation.
- If the upgrade changes cloud-init/user-data for nodes, note that immutability of OS images may require reprovisioning nodes (plan for capacity).

kubeadm / version compatibility quick reference:
- kubeadm v1.27 supports control-plane upgrades from 1.25+ (verify patch matrix in docs).
- kubelet is allowed up to one minor version skew (kubelet <= control-plane + 1).
- For major migrations (e.g., 1.24 -> 1.27), perform in two steps (1.24->1.26, then 1.26->1.27).

Commands and snippets (examples):
- etcd snapshot:
  ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=${ETCD_ENDPOINTS} snapshot save /tmp/backup-$(date +%F).db --cacert=/etc/etcd/pki/ca.crt --cert=/etc/etcd/pki/client.crt --key=/etc/etcd/pki/client.key

- kubeadm upgrade plan:
  kubeadm upgrade plan

- upgrade control-plane on a master node (example):
  ssh core@cp-01
  sudo systemctl stop kubelet
  sudo kubeadm upgrade apply v1.27.3 -y
  sudo systemctl start kubelet

- drain node safely:
  kubectl drain worker-xx --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --pod-selector='!critical'

- terraform plan with var file:
  terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars -out=plan-prod.tfplan

Validation checks (post-upgrade):
- kubectl get nodes -> Ready status across all nodes
- kubectl get cs or kubectl get componentstatuses (note: may be deprecated; prefer checking pods in kube-system)
- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | grep -E "CrashLoopBackOff|ImagePullBackOff"
- API server latency check: curl to /healthz and /readyz with timing, run 5x, compare to baseline
- etcd member health: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=... endpoint health

Rollback strategies (several levels):
A) Fast revert (control-plane minor failure during kubeadm apply):
  - If API server not healthy after kubeadm apply and errors indicate manifest mismatch, revert kubeadm by reapplying previous kubeadm config (keep backup of /etc/kubernetes/manifests) and restart kubelet; restore etcd snapshot if dataloss suspected.
B) Node-level rollback: reprovision node from previous image template using terraform (module supports reprovision flag).
C) Full cluster restore: restore etcd snapshot to a fresh control-plane using bootstrap token and run kubeadm init --config with previous version.

vSphere-specific considerations:
- vSphere tools and VMware guest customization can add a 1-2 minute delay on first boot; allow longer timeouts in probes for newly provisioned VMs.
- Use vm-templates that match cloud-init/user-data expectations. Avoid template rebuilds mid-upgrade.
- When resizing disks for kubelet eviction thresholds, prefer offline resize + reboot.
- Watch for vCenter tasks backlog; parallel node reboots > 8 can saturate vCenter task queue.

Bare-metal-specific considerations:
- PXE/iPXE timeouts: ensure TFTP server can serve concurrent nodes (increase threads if >10 nodes reprovisioning).
- Firmware and driver compatibility: check NIC drivers (intel igb/ixgbe) versions against kernel used by image.
- Power control: integrate with IPMI/Redfish provider defined in terraform; ensure BMC credentials in secrets manager are valid.

Canary/Gradual strategies:
- Use a spare node-pool (spare_node_pool_size) to upgrade small batch (e.g., 2 nodes) and run smoke tests for 30 minutes before continuing.
- For control-plane upgrades, first upgrade single control-plane member in an odd-size cluster (3/5) and validate leader election and etcd quorum.

Smoke test checklist (automatable):
- simple app deployment (nginx with 3 replicas) -> verify readiness and response codes
- embedding API synthetic request through Redwood runtime -> verify latency within X% of baseline
- create/delete PVCs to validate storage provisioning and CSI drivers post-upgrade

Monitoring and observability during upgrade:
- Ensure kube-state-metrics and Prometheus scrape targets are healthy.
- Keep Grafana dashboard open (control-plane, apiserver latency, etcd commit latency) and record spikes.

Known open questions / TODOs:
- TODO: finalize terraform module variable name parity between vsphere-hosts and baremetal-provisioner (currently: vm_template vs image_template).
- TODO: add automated preflight script that runs all pre-checks and uploads results to ticket artifact. (PR: github/terraform-modules #82)
- QUESTION: do we standardize on Calico IPIP vs VXLAN for cross-datacenter clusters? Impact on MTU and CNI upgrade path. Need security input.
- TODO: add a documented, automated etcd restore test in CI (nightly) to guarantee snapshot usability.

Post-mortem capture template (for failed upgrades):
- Summary of event, timeline, and immediate remediation steps taken.
- Root cause analysis (component-level).
- Action items: terraform module fixes, image updates, runbook clarifications, SRE training.

Appendix: quick recovery commands (copy into terminal during incident)
- Restore etcd snapshot to temp-dir and list snapshot info:
  ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot status /tmp/backup.db

- Restore snapshot to cluster (example skeleton):
  ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore /tmp/backup.db --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-from-backup --name=etcd-restore-1 --initial-cluster="etcd-restore-1=http://127.0.0.1:2380" --initial-cluster-token=restore-token

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight, move long Terraform module design discussion to a design doc under product/ or infra/ once module APIs stabilize.

References and links:
- Kubernetes upgrade docs: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubeadm/kubeadm-upgrade/
- Redwood internal terraform modules: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules (see vsphere-hosts, private-k8s-cluster)
- Etcd backup best practices: https://etcd.io/docs/v3.5/op-guide/snapshot/

End of draft.

Change log (recent):
- 2026-02-24: added vsphere note about vCenter task queue limits (Miguel).
- 2026-03-05: added terraform module variable notes and open TODOs (Ethan).
